title: Offline-first edge routing idea pad
content:
Quick brain dump for an offline-first / intermittent-connectivity inference routing idea. Goal is a lightweight developer-facing pattern that makes LLM-powered mobile experiences robust when connectivity is poor, without forcing teams to manage a full on-device model or complex private deployment. Treating this as a personal scratchpad — lots of open questions.

Problem space
- Mobile apps (productivity, field-sales, diagnostics, healthcare data capture) need helpful model responses even when connectivity is intermittent or high-latency.
- Full on-device models are heavy, and customers may not want to ship model weights. Private deployments are heavy ops for smaller teams.
- Users degrade into bad experience when requests time out or switch to a low-quality fallback without preserving context.

Hypothesis
- A hybrid "edge routing" layer (client + small persisted cache + lightweight local execution hooks) can deliver acceptable quality on intermittent connectivity by combining: (a) on-device prompt templates + cached KV/prefix, (b) small policy engine to choose local heuristics vs remote call, (c) opportunistic sync and background prefetch of likely-needed context.
- Outcome: fewer visible failures, lower p99 latency in poor networks, reduced token spend for redundant remote calls.

MVP scope (developer-facing product)
- Client SDK additions (JS/Android/iOS):
  - Simple config: {offline_mode: boolean, cache_ttl: ms, fallback_policy: [cached_response | local_template | background_retry]}
  - Local cache: prefix cache (conversation slices) + last-good-response store with metadata (model, model-version, prompt-hash)
  - Policy hook: small deterministic decision function (connectivity check + latency threshold + cached relevance score) exposed to app devs
- Server-side: routing endpoint that accepts an "edge-hint" header and supports lightweight prefetch endpoints (prefetch manifest for user/session)
- docs: short guide + examples (chat app, form autofill, diagnostic checklist)

User stories
- As a mobile product engineer, I want users to still get reasonable suggestions when a network is flaky, so retention and trust stay high.
- As an app user (field agent), I need the app to return the last helpful assistant answer offline rather than failing silently.
- As infra, I want to reduce redundant repeated token spend when the app keeps retrying during a transient outage.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- SDK exposes a one-line opt-in into offline routing with reasonable defaults.
- When device reports no connectivity, SDK uses cached response if relevance > 0.7 OR falls back to template answer with clear UX badge ("offline suggestion").
- Server exposes a prefetch manifest endpoint; sample app demonstrates background prefetch of top-3 likely prompt prefixes.
- Telemetry: p99 response time improved for flaky networks, offline-success-rate metric captured, and token spend for retried calls reduced by >20% in an internal pilot.

API sketches / config
- POST /v1/edge/prefetch-manifest (auth) -> {prefixes: [string], ttl_sec: 3600}
- Client config:
  {
    offline_mode: true,
    cache_ttl_ms: 3600000,
    fallback_order: ["cached_response","local_template","degraded_stub"],
    relevancy_threshold: 0.7
  }
- SDK decides: if (navigator.online == false) -> try cached_response => if relevancy < threshold -> local_template
- telemetry events: edge.cache_hit, edge.cache_miss, edge.offline_fallback_used, edge.prefetch_success

UX ideas
- Small badge on response: "offline suggestion" with timestamp and a button "Send when online" to queue a server-eval.
- Developer can opt into two UX modes: optimistic (show offline suggestion as primary) vs conservative (show 'limited' message with option to retry).

Metrics to track (experiment)
- Offline-success-rate: percent of offline requests that return a suggestion instead of an error.
- User-accept-rate: percent of offline suggestions that users accept or act on.
- Token-savings-per-session: tokens saved from avoiding redundant retries.
- Background-prefetch-success-rate: percent of prefetched prefixes that are used within TTL.

Privacy / Security considerations
- Cached content may include PII; default SDK should encrypt local cache with platform keystore and provide opt-out hooks.
- For enterprise/private customers, allow a policy that disables prefetching or local caching entirely (compliance).

Risks and unknowns
- Relevance scoring on cached prefixes: how to compute cheaply on-device? Need lightweight embedding or heuristic scoring.
- UX: showing stale or incorrect info could erode trust. Must label and provide easy retry paths.
- Storage: mobile storage limits; TTLs and eviction policies need careful defaults.

Implementation experiments (short list)
1) Heuristic baseline: timestamped last-good-response + n-gram overlap to compute simple relevance; fast and no model weights.
2) On-device tiny embedder: test a 16MB quantized embedder for cheap similarity. Evaluate accuracy vs size.
3) Prefetch pilot: server computes top-3 prefixes from user activity graph and pushes manifest to client during active sessions.

Milestones (quarterly rough)
- Week 0-4: prototype SDK hooks, basic cache, simple heuristic relevance for Android + web sample app.
- Week 5-8: prefetch manifest API + server integration + small internal pilot with mobile team.
- Week 9-12: metrics collection, iterate on UX messaging, decide on on-device embedder experiment.

Open questions / TODOs
- How do we compute relevancy without embeddings on-device? (TODO: spike n-gram heuristic)
- Should we support model-variant hints (e.g., if cached response used was from a higher-cost model, should we downgrade?)
- Which enterprise controls needed to disable caching/prefetch? (policy schema)
- Billing implications: how to attribute server-side prefetch work vs immediate calls?

Next steps (for me)
- Create JIRA epic INF-EDGE-OFFLINE and add tickets for SDK + server prefet ch API + metrics.
- Sync with mobile SDK leads (Ravi) and platform infra (Lena) to validate encryption and storage plan.
- Quick spike: implement n-gram relevance prototype in mobile sample app by 10/20.

Notes to self: keep the initial interface extremely simple — opt-in boolean + two thresholds. Avoid pushing on-device ML until we know product/UX benefit. Also document default TTLs and eviction behavior for the pilot so infra can estimate storage and network cost.

References/links: sample pilot app repo (github:redwood/edge-offline-sample), Confluence sketch (confluence:EDGE-offline-notes), related JIRA INF-2319 (edge prefetch).
